RFC: his inbox, agent to him

An agent asks him something only once a check has proved that only he can answer it, and the ask arrives ready: what it is, why him, the agent's pick and a link to the thing itself.

  1. Draft
  2. Review
  3. Accepted
  4. Shipped
  • For: Nicolas, who reads his inbox and sets how much it shows; the tasks that build it, rust-inbox-triage first.
  • Goal: nothing reaches /inbox that is settled, not his, held behind a gate of his, or not ready to answer.
  • Status: accepted. His one decision is in: at most 7 asks shown at once (section 7; @nha, 2026-11-11: « 7 s fine. »). The build starts from it.

1. Intent

Writer notes
  • His brief, 2026-11-11, verbatim: « /inbox "72 things wait on Nicolas" - too many and how many are really needing me ? », « we need to treat this as the reverse pendant of the comments. Comments = me to agent. /inbox = agent to me. there needs to be a "backlog" of things an agent / JEV has to double-check that they truly need me. We need to start building the rules now as we find it, as well as the logic (state similar to tasks?). », « the presentation is also terrible right now », « it is clear that the things put in front of me are not ready to review or approve. Please add a design doc (light RFC) about how to handle my inbox. »
  • Intent only (rfc skill, rule 2): no tool, file or number here.
  • Rules carry r- ids while at Review: design_rules_test fails on a rule- id no test holds. Once accepted, rust-inbox-triage and rust-inbox-page rename each to rule- in the PR that adds its test (rfc skill, rule 29).
  1. Only what needs him. An ask he sees is one no agent can answer, not already settled, and not behind a gate he named.
    • Testable: every ask shown names the reason only he can answer it, from a short fixed list.
  2. Ready in one look. He can answer an ask from its line and its link, with no search and no question back.
  3. Approved means done by an agent. Once he approves, the thing goes out without him; when no tool can send it, the ask says why and holds everything he needs.
  4. Rules grow as cases appear. Each case that should not have reached him becomes a rule with a test, so the same kind never reaches him again.
  5. An ask has a life, as a task does. Its state is known, every move has an owner, and nothing waits forever unseen.
  6. The page reads like a short to-do. One line per ask, its action and its link; no warning, raw id or pasted text.

2. The mirror of comments

Writer notes
  • @nha, 2026-11-11: « Comments = me to agent. /inbox = agent to me. »
  • The comment side is as built: the watcher routes a comment to its task's card (rfc-project-boards section 10), and the comment resolves when that task merges (task comment-task-status, done).

A comment and an ask are the same flow, run in opposite directions. Each has a sender, a router, a place it lands and an answer that closes it. Comments already have every part; asks lack the router that checks them, so everything raised lands on him.

CommentAsk
SenderNicolasAn agent, a task, the PM loop, the mail poll
RouterThe watcher: picks the task's cardThe check pass: drops, holds or shows
Lands onThe task's card, its agent woken/inbox, one line
Answered byAn agent, in the threadNicolas: a button, or a comment on the ask
Closes whenIts task mergesThe asker acted on his answer, or a rule settled it

The two meet at one point: a comment he writes on an ask (« not mine », « held on CAPE ») is routed like any comment, to the check pass, which turns it into a rule.

3. The ask and its states

Writer notes
  • @nha, 2026-11-11: « as well as the logic (state similar to tasks?) ». The states are the brief's six: raised, checked, held, shown, answered, dropped.
  • Why asks piled up (private/notes/inbox-triage-rules.md, « mechanism faults »): the PM loop wrote waiting lines for work never his; nothing closed a waiting line when its PR merged, its message went or its lead dropped; the inbox script refused to take a waiting file; two readers disagreed on what is open. One record with one state fixes all four: one writer, one reader, closed by events.
  • Counts: /inbox read « 71 things wait on Nicolas » on 2026-11-11 before a triage pass by hand and 25 after it (curl -s -H 'accept: text/plain' http://127.0.0.1:7788/inbox | grep 'things wait', same day); 45 of the 48 asks from other sessions were already settled.

An ask is one record in the store, as a task is, with one state. Every source writes asks through the same command; nothing else lands on /inbox.

StateMeansWho moves it out, to where
raisedAn agent wrote it; nobody checked it yetThe check pass: to checked, held or dropped; or back to its asker, still raised, with what the readiness bar found missing
checkedPassed the bar, truly his, waiting for its turn on the pageThe app: to shown, in order of deadline then age (section 7)
heldHis, but behind a gate of his; prepared, never shownThe app, when the gate lifts: back to raised, so the check runs again on fresh facts
shownOn /inbox nowNicolas: to answered. A rule that fires meanwhile (PR merged, message sent): to dropped
answeredHe answered; the asker is woken with his wordsThe asker acts; the record keeps his answer, so it is never asked again
droppedSettled, not his, or an agent can do itFinal. Each drop names its rule; the page folds a day's drops away for trust

4. The readiness bar

Writer notes
  • @nha, 2026-11-11: « it is clear that the things put in front of me are not ready to review or approve »; on Shani: « how does the /mail link help me ? »; « Datadog: unclear what I need to do. »; on Mirakl: « it says "approved" if it really is why do you ask ? If it is then where is the CV ? and the presentation is very sub-par on this page still »; « I approved so this is up to you to send automatically. You should have credentials. »; « I need a link. »
  • The approved free-work forms went out through freework_apply.py's API the same day (commit 9b43d44ea, applications 10599014 and 10599020): the rule « a form on someone else's site stays his » had handed them to him.

An ask carries five fields, each required when it is raised; the check pass refuses an ask with one empty or weak, and sends it back to its asker.

  1. What it is, in plain words. One line he could act on without the agent's context: no task id, no file path, no pasted mail.
    • Jev scores the line for plain words, as dash doc ready scores a doc; under the bar, it goes back.
  2. Why only him. One reason from a fixed list, never free text:
    • outside party: a decision that commits him to someone (a call, a contract, a rate).
    • wording: new words in his voice, only the new blocks of a draft.
    • his hands: a browser sign-in, sudo, the keychain, a form on a site with no stored credentials.
    • one way: an irreversible choice that is contested.
  3. The agent's pick. What the agent would do, so his answer can be « yes ».
  4. A link that opens the thing itself. The mail thread, the draft, the form, the PR; never a list page such as /mail. The link must answer before the ask is shown.
  5. For an approval: who sends it. The tool that sends it once he says yes. Else the reason no tool can, and every piece he needs, linked: the form, the CV PDF, the message to copy.
Approved thingSent by, after his yesTask
Maildash mail send, from nicolas@klar.imexists
LinkedIn messageThe LinkedIn tool, on a slow random watchapproved-send-watch
Free-work applicationFree-work's API, the CV shared in the same callfreework-apply-shares-cv
Greenhouse form (Mirakl)A headless browser with its own profilerust-apply-greenhouse, first use apply-mirakl
LinkedIn Easy ApplyThe app's Easy Apply, on his approvalexists
Any other formNo tool yet: the ask links form, CV and text, and a task to build the tool is raised in the same moveone per site

An approved item never comes back to him as an ask to approve. If it sits approved and unsent, that is an agent's failure, raised to the orchestrator, not to him.

5. The check pass and its rules

Writer notes
  • @nha, 2026-11-11: « there needs to be a "backlog" of things an agent / JEV has to double-check that they truly need me. We need to start building the rules now as we find it ».
  • The first rules are private/notes/inbox-triage-rules.md, found on 2026-11-11 by the triage pass by hand. They move into the rules file in rust-inbox-triage's first PR; the note then points to it.
  • Global rule: a new check needs a test and a count of its firings, or it is dead weight. The firing count is the reason each rule keeps a counter.

The check pass runs on every raised ask, again on every event a rule watches (a PR merged, a draft sent, a lead dropped, a gate lifted), and on each orchestrator tick. It works in three steps, cheapest first.

  1. Rules, in code. Each rule is a row of data: a kind, a test against the store, his words, an example ask and the verdict it must give. Most asks end here, at no cost.
  2. Jev, for words. Scores the « what » line for plain words and asks « could an agent do this? ». Cheap; a low score sends the ask back.
  3. An agent, for the rest. An ask no rule decides and Jev doubts goes to the orchestrator's check. Its verdict must cite a rule, or add one in the same change.
KindVerdictFirst rows
settleddroppedIts PR merged or closed; its task done; its approval tapped; its draft sent, moot or its lead dropped; superseded by a settled ask; a sudo run whose check passes
neverdroppedA paid or sales pitch; an optional step nothing depends on; an after-merge check or a reviewer resuming (section 6)
heldheldAnything for Babel while the CAPE contract is unsigned
hischeckedThe four reasons of the bar
# one rule, a row of the tracked rules file beside the check's code
[[rule]]
id      = "never-pitch"
kind    = "never"          # settled | never | held | his
when    = "source-is-pitch" # a test the check's code defines
said    = "@nha, 2026-11-11: « ignore all these paid pitches as a rule »"
example = { source = "crisp", title = "Collab x Max Zaharenkov (#146)" }
expect  = "dropped"
  1. A rule without its example fails the build. One table test runs every row's example and checks its verdict, so each rule has its test by construction.
  2. A rule counts its firings. dash inbox rules prints each rule with its count; a rule at zero for a month is proposed for removal.
  3. His « not mine » is a rule waiting to be written. His comment on a shown ask drops it now, and the next check pass writes the rule it implies, with his words in said.
Why rows of data and not a prompt

A prompt cannot be tested row by row and drifts with the model. A row has an example and a verdict, so a broken rule shows in CI, and a count shows a rule that never fires. New kinds of test against the store (a new when) are Rust code with their own test; most new rules reuse an existing one.

6. Held, and never his

Writer notes
  • @nha, 2026-11-11: « Babel stuff is all blocked on the contract CAPE. We can prepare but not act yet. So prepare but don't ask me. »
  • @nha, 2026-11-11: « ignore all these paid pitches as a rule. This is something to improve in Klar if this wasn't marked marketing, and in perso if it was and you ask me anyway ». Klar's side is klar-582.
  • « Datadog: unclear what I need to do. »: the Datadog plugin sign-in was optional, nothing depended on it; it falls under never his.

Held behind his gates

A gate is a record: its name, his words, what it holds, and the fact that lifts it. Agents keep preparing behind it: drafts written, blocks proposed, each ask raised and held. None reaches him.

GateHoldsLifts when
CAPEEvery ask about Babel Coop: its drafts, its blocks, the Hostman account questionThe CAPE contract is signed, recorded in the store from its mail or his word
A dateAn ask that cannot act before a day (the graal Developer ID, from 2027-01-04)The day comes

When a gate lifts, its asks go back to raised and are checked again: weeks behind a gate can settle or stale them.

Never his

  1. A paid or sales pitch. Dropped, never asked. In Klar's mail, a pitch is marked marketing by its classifier (klar-582); here, a pitch that reaches the check anyway is dropped by rule, and that rule's firing is a Klar miss to report.
  2. An optional step nothing depends on. Dropped; if something later depends on it, that dependency raises it again with the reason.
  3. An after-merge check, a reviewer resuming, an agent's own follow-up. The orchestrator's from the start; the PM loop never raises them as asks.
  4. A comment waiting on Claude. An agent's queue, not his; it lives on the agents' side, never on /inbox.
  5. An approved thing to send. An agent sends it (the bar).

7. The page

Writer notes
  • @nha, 2026-11-11: « the presentation is also terrible right now », « I need a link. »
  • On 2026-11-11, /inbox mixed warnings, raw draft ids, three comments waiting on Claude, 12 lines of Babel blocks, two pasted texts from other sessions, and the whole daily list below.
  • Components only from /design (rust/CLAUDE.md rule 6): List with Item rows (look issue-row), Badge, Button, Fold. One primary action per view, the rest neutral (/design's Directing rules).
  1. The count is the shown asks. Never the raised, held or dropped ones.
  2. Grouped by what he does: Approve, Decide, Do. Inside a group, nearest deadline first, then oldest.
  3. One row per ask: the plain-words line as title; why him and the agent's pick on the second line; the whole row links to the thing itself.
  4. Answer in place. An approval row's button approves; any row takes a comment (« not mine », « later »), routed like any comment.
  5. Two folds: held, by gate; dropped today, each with its rule. They are there for trust, closed by default.
  6. Nothing else. No warning, raw id or pasted text (those go back to the check pass), no comments waiting on Claude, no daily list (it lives on /today). The text form, for agents, lists the same rows at the same URL.
decided How many asks should /inbox show at once? A, at most 7 (@nha, 2026-11-11: « 7 s fine. »)
OptionWhat changes for youCost or riskOur call
A. At most 7, the rest wait their turnNever more than 7 lines. When you answer one, the next ready one takes its place. The heading says how many more wait, without listing them.A ready ask can wait a day for its turn. A deadline within 48 hours jumps the line, so nothing urgent waits.Pick: a short list you can clear in one sitting, and the order says what matters first.
B. Everything that passed the checkEvery ready ask at once, however many a busy day brings.Nothing waits for a slot, but a long day looks like today's page again.Not picked: the check cuts what is not yours, not how much is.
C. One batch a day, at a set hourThe page fills once a day, say 9:00, and stays still until the next day.A reply that comes at 10:00 waits a day; a call slot can be lost.Not picked: replies to people lose a day.

8. Who builds what

Writer notes
  • Links are /tasks/<id> on the main app, as the brief asks; a non-Rust task redirects to its issue view. Klar's task is on Klar's board.
  • Port, then fix (CLAUDE.md, Coordination 5): the record replaces the inbox parts of Elixir's Dashboard.Handoff and Dashboard.NeedsYou and the waiting lines of agent_inbox.py; nothing is fixed in Elixir.

Phases order the build: the record and the check first, since the page shows only what the check lets through.

DecisionTask

The page, groups, rows, folds, the cap (7)rust-inbox-page, after rust-inbox-triage
A link that opens the thing itself, here and in each turn's « What you need to do » (bar 4)rust-needs-you-links
An ask raised from a task says its intent in plain words (bar 1)task-plan-required
Approved means sent (bar 5)rust-apply-greenhouse, freework-apply-shares-cv, approved-send-watch; Mirakl through apply-mirakl

10. Glossary

Writer notes

TermMeaningSource
AskSomething an agent needs from him, one record with one state; the reverse of a comment. Checked by the check pass.@nha, 2026-11-11: « /inbox = agent to me »
Check passWhat decides whether an ask reaches him: rules first, then Jev, then an agent.This doc, section 5
RuleA row of data the check pass runs: kind, test, his words, an example and its verdict.private/notes/inbox-triage-rules.md
